segments.text: Concretely, the SDK hashes the longest matching prefix of the request and looks it up; only the suffix past the last cache breakpoint is recomputed.
So reordering a prompt so the stable system text leads and the volatile user turn trails is what actually lands cache hits — not shrinking the payload.
Prompt caching is prefix-based, not content-based: a cache hit needs the leading tokens to match byte-for-byte, in order.
You measure it from the response usage block: cache_read_input_tokens counts the prefix served from cache, cache_creation_input_tokens the part freshly written.
